blind.why: Main menu 1920 vs real CS2 main menu (Steam community capture). Ours has the clearer hierarchy: one obvious PLAY CTA, visible match setup, lit team line-up on a reflective floor. CS2 stages one hero character better. Ours shows identical clones in the same aim pose, and hard-edged grey and orange rectangles float in the backdrop.

Settings (Controls) 1920 vs CS2 Advanced Video. CS2's rows are large and legible, it has a live preview image and hover tooltips that explain each option, and it marks recommended values. Our modal is clean but sparse: about 500px of dead space between each label and its control, sub-labels are 13px grey on dark, there are no explanations or previews, and the content is cut off at the bottom with no scroll cue.

Crosshair tab 1920 vs CS2 Crosshair settings. Ours is the more capable designer: swatches with hex entry, live preview with background and movement states, share code and presets. CS2's preview uses real map backdrops, while ours is a toy sky gradient with an illegible LIVE PREVIEW label. Geometry sliders stay active for the Dot style, where CS2 greys them out.

Match-end recap (real match:end, 1920) vs CS2 match result. CS2 is a ceremony: VICTORY banner, team score medallions, players standing in the scene, award cards. Ours is two flat tables and a one-line MVP strip, with about 430px of empty screen between the MVP strip and the Play again and Main menu buttons.

biggest_gap: The settings sheet is the screen players use most, and it is not up to CS2. (1) At 1280x720 the Crosshair tab's Length, Gap and Thickness sliders shrink to 42px tracks (measured with getBoundingClientRect; 149px at 1920), so they are unusable. The FT-… share code is clipped, and Outline and Dynamic spread fall below the fold with no scroll cue (shots/critic-menu-r2/f_settings-crosshair_1280.png). (2) At 1920 every tab is a sparse two-column list: labels at the far left, controls about 500px away at the far right, 13px low-contrast sub-labels, and rows cut off at the bottom edge (b02_settings_open_1920.png, pair2.png). Repro: normal URL, then Settings, then Crosshair at 1280x720. CS2 instead uses full-width rows with large type, a hover tooltip for every option, a live preview and recommended-value markers. Fix: give the control column a minimum width (sliders at least 160px), stack the preview under the controls below about 1400px, add a bottom fade and scroll cue, and add per-row help or tooltips.
other_gaps: The match-end recap is thin: no characters, no award cards, no per-player highlight. It leaves about 40% of the screen empty between the MVP strip and the buttons at 1920 (d_end_1920.png). CS2 stages the winners in the scene with award cards.

Keyboard focus is lost. After Esc closes Settings, focus goes to <body> instead of back to the Settings item. The pause menu also opens with focus on <body> (Resume is never focused, despite data-autofocus). Hovering Play leaves a stale focus highlight on a second menu item, so two rows are lit at once (a07_hover_play_1280.png).

The Resume button shows an 'Esc' key hint. In real Chrome, Escape is not a user-activation key, so requestPointerLock from Esc will fail and the pause reopens 350ms later. Headless Chrome hides this, so it is unverified. Drop the Esc hint or resume with a click-to-capture prompt.

Backdrop polish: hard-edged floating grey quads and pink light-shaft slabs show at the top of the frame, six identical clones share one pose (two are half-hidden behind the setup card), and the big ring arc cuts through the 'COMPETITIVE TAG SPORT' tagline.

Boot and backdrop cost: page load to main menu took 57–230s under SwiftShader, and the menu rAF ran at 1.3fps while gameplay was faster. The splash meanwhile shows only a logo and a 40px line with no progress, so on weak GPUs it looks hung. Show real progress and a low-cost backdrop fallback.
The viewmodel preview is a schematic gun on a flat sky. The tutorial card touches or overlaps the radar's location label at HUD scale 130% (b07_ingame_1920.png), and it stays up through roundEnd.
bugs: Console error in the first-run flow: cosmetics/ui/styles.js still requests fonts.googleapis.com (REQFAIL / ERR_CERT_AUTHORITY_INVALID) when the Locker opens from the menu.
1280x720 Crosshair tab: geometry sliders are 42px wide and the share-code field is clipped.
Focus is not restored after closing an overlay, and the pause menu opens with no focused element.
Locker opened from the main menu in live (non-test) runs showed an empty, black character preview in 3 of 3 attempts. In test mode it renders, so this may be SwiftShader starvation (unverified).
strengths: Round-1 blockers are fixed. The HUD is hidden under pause, settings-from-pause and the end screen (html.fx-nohud). The tutorial card is docked left-middle and hides under overlays. Esc closes settings even from inside the callsign input. Pause releases pointer lock, Resume re-locks it, and Esc in game opens pause.

Settings apply for real. FOV 120 gives a camera hfov of 120.0°. Crosshair Dot applies in game. HUD scale 130% visibly scales the HUD. The pause quick sensitivity slider changes settings.sensitivity (1→1.05). Rebinding Move forward to I writes keybinds.forward=['KeyI'].

Full flow works with no stuck states: boot → main → Play (Enter or click) → buy phase with 10 actors → pause → settings → leave confirm (Stay/Leave) → main in about 10s (backdrop restored) → locker → back to main → real match:end → recap with Play again / Main menu.
The main menu is attractive and has a clear hierarchy. The crosshair designer is richer than CS2's.
